note: THE DOCUMENTATION EXISTS AND NOTHING LINKED TO IT. Harvest's docs are live at docs.theharvest.site - 24 pages across six sections plus a changelog - and neither product pointed at them. The founder asked for a link in the app 'above or under billing'. It went UNDER Billing & Payments, in the admin account menu, ungated. Nothing else in this repo changed: the nav rail, its four flyouts, the REACH group, MORE_GROUPS, the mobile bottom nav and the More sheet are untouched, as are firestore.rules, firestore.indexes.json, functions/ and layout.tsx. No npm dependency was added, no theme token was minted, and all 43 installed primitives are byte-identical.

entries.why: GAINED ONE UNGATED ROW, AND EVERY ROW GAINED THE TOUCH FLOOR. The row is Documentation, an <a> to docs.theharvest.site with target=_blank and rel=noopener, sitting DIRECTLY BELOW Billing & Payments - the founder offered 'above or under' and under is the answer, because Billing is a destructive-adjacent destination people reach by muscle memory and a new row above it moves a target they already know at the one moment that matters. It is an anchor rather than a button with a handler so middle-click, ctrl-click and open-in-new-tab all still work, and its onClick only closes the menu. It carries NO entitlement condition, unlike Settings and Billing above it: every admin can read the docs, so there is nothing to gate and a row that appeared only for owners would be the docs hidden behind billing. THE FLOOR IS THE SECOND HALF AND IT FIXES A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT, measured in real Chromium with animation suppressed: every row in this menu was 40px below sm (under the 44px touch floor) and 36.25px at 1024 and above (under Rule 4's own 38px control floor), because px-4 py-2.5 around text-sm computes to that and globals.css trims the rem base above 1024. A dropdown row is a tap target. Rather than add a seventh row that misses both floors, the six class strings were consolidated into one shared ROW constant carrying min-h-11 - 44px below sm and 39.875px above, inside Rule 4's band, which is the same figure THE-334 measured for this component's own rail trigger, so ONE token serves both floors and no sm: variant is needed. The shared string is also what keeps THE-181's w-full requirement true of a row added later. No permission, no handler, no existing row, no variant and no placement changed; the panel is still w-60 and the rail still opens upward.

APPENDED TO, NEVER SUBSTITUTED - the population of suites pinning firestore.rules went 70 -> 71 because THE-358 adds a suite that pins it, and this ticket's row was added to RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE beside THE-357's rather than over it. The floor is EXACT by design and may not shrink, so a new pinner has to be recorded here or section 5 fails; that is the register working, not an obstacle to it. THE-358's entry names what its suite still asserts, in the form every entry above it uses. THE-325's own PINNING_SUITES moved with it, since two mechanisms counting one population is how one of them comes to be wrong. Nothing else in this file changed: no accepted digest was replaced, no assertion was loosened, and this ticket records NO firestore.rules digest of its own - it adds one <a> to the documentation site and opens no read, no write and no collection, which is the register's rule for a ticket that does not touch the file.
